inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average DILUTED count from the H1 FY2026 interim EPS note (264,898,646 issued + 28,635,139 dilutive Stock Incentive Plan options, treasury-stock method; 35,575,224 options outstanding at HK$1.10-12.40). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so no further dilution is charged. Issued shares alone are 264.9m; using the diluted figure is the conservative choice given the options are mostly in the money even at the current price.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share based payment' RMB11,464k (line 4839); no net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). H1 FY2026 SBC was RMB942k.
inputs.interest_income_note: RMB19.406m is the income-statement interest income (FY2025 AR note 5, line 6585), which is the figure the Metrics EBITDA was derived from; the cash-flow reconciliation line shows only RMB5.962m because the balance is interest on financial assets at amortised cost. The larger figure is stripped because all of its source assets (cash, FVTPL wealth-management products, amortised-cost products) are credited in the bridge. FY2025 fair-value gains on FVTPL products (RMB53.1m) are likewise excluded from the EBITDA base.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow 'Shares repurchased' RMB18,063k (806,800 shares); zero in H1 FY2026. The company has never paid a dividend. The flat count is therefore mostly a modelling convention, not a funded policy.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1721 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-10T03:38Z. All per-share values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1721 to the HKD quote basis; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD, the _cny twins are RMB. No dual listing exists for a parity check; direction verified by the July-2025 placing (HK$106.60 = RMB286.965m / 3.0m shares = RMB95.66 -> 1.114 then, consistent with CNY/HKD in the 1.08-1.18 range).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in the flows' currency (CNY): 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8%, China ERP ~6.5-7.0%, beta ~1.2 for a project-based B2B marketing-services small-cap, no debt benefit assumed (net cash). Cost of equity ~10%; WACC 10.0% applied to every scenario. Governance, customer-concentration and cash-repatriation risks are charged ONCE, through the scenario probability weights (bear 40%), not through a WACC premium and not through per-scenario WACC differences.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (FY2025 principal RMB2,977k + interest RMB175k = RMB3.2m, 0.19% of revenue) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path 0.2%; lease liabilities (RMB4.7m at 30 Jun 2026) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (PP&E depreciation RMB49.5m = 2.98% of FY2025 revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled whole-group; the NCI stock (RMB1.347m at 30 Jun 2026, down from RMB29.3m after the FY2025 RMB120m buyout of the minority) is deducted once in the equity bridge. Not charged in the flows. FY0 tie: EBIT 272m x (1-11.4%) = 241m vs attributable NI 285.7m less non-operating items (FV gains 53.1 + interest 19.4 - finance costs 17.5 = +55) = 231m, within noise.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: B2B marketing services delivered through an owned network of AI interactive vending/marketing terminals in mainland China, plus merchandise sales through the same terminals). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (non-US operating company) with the adaptations file applied: CNY/HKD dual currency, treatment-B leases, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for stripped interest and FV income, SBC-light market. First valuation of this ticker (no prior Drivers/DCF, no memory entry). EBITDA basis: PBT + finance costs - interest income - FVTPL fair-value gains + D&A + SBC = FY2025 RMB336.5m (20.2%), FY2024 ~RMB337m (25.2%), H1 FY2026 ~RMB207m (25.1%, S&D expenses +7% on revenue +22%). FY2025 reported FCF of RMB358m was flattered by an RMB85m unwind of prepayments; the component build starts from a ~14% owner-FCF margin, not the 19.7% headline. One-offs excluded from the base: FY2024 RMB1,899m non-cash fair-value loss on pre-IPO preferred shares converted at the May-2024 IPO (why FY2024 statutory NI was -1,672m and FY2023 equity negative), FY2024 listing expenses. Only two clean annual periods exist (FY2024, FY2025) so every mid-cycle assumption is set conservatively against that thin history. PRICE CONTEXT: the stock has fallen ~95% from the July-2025 placing (HK$106.60, market HK$128.50) to HK$6.6 in a continuous year-long slide on heavy volume, with no split, suspension, profit warning or subsequent event disclosed; at this price the issued-share market cap (~HK$1.75bn) is BELOW net cash plus wealth-management products (RMB1,434m ~ HK$1.68bn), i.e. enterprise value is roughly zero against ~RMB300m of annual owner FCF. The model cannot reconcile that price with the accounts as filed; see valuation_philosophy. Price is a Friday regular close, not after-hours.

H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet, 30 Jun 2026; source of the stripped amortised-cost interest income.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 year-1 base growth, anchored to H1 FY2026 +22.2% with harder H2 comparatives; the house default (equity CAGR) is undefined for this ticker
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not computable: equity was negative through FY2023 (-387.8m) because pre-IPO convertible redeemable preferred shares sat in liabilities until the May-2024 IPO conversion, and FY2024/FY2025 equity was built by IPO/placing proceeds, not retained earnings. EPS 2-yr CAGR (-7%) is distorted by the IPO share count increase and FY2024 is negative. Revenue (FY2023->FY2025 28.5%, FY2022->FY2025 44.3% on a partial FY2022 row) and owner FCF (FY2023 141.4 -> FY2024 105.3 -> FY2025 327.2, 52% 2-yr CAGR, the FY2025 figure inflated by an RMB85m prepayment unwind) are the only usable series, and both cover two full years post-IPO. Treat all historical CAGRs as low-confidence.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history: FY2023 156.2-14.6-0.2 = 141.4; FY2024 127.1-17.6-4.2 = 105.3; FY2025 358.1-11.5-19.4 = 327.2 (RMB m). SBC is shrinking as a share of revenue (1.5% -> 1.3% -> 0.7%, 0.1% in H1 FY2026), so SBC is not eating the FCF growth; working capital (131-day DSO on trade receivables of RMB599m at FY2025, RMB672m at H1 FY2026, with RMB35m/yr ECL charges) is the real drag on cash conversion.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +20% (H1 +22.2%, brand customers +57%, AI interactive +102%, KA ARPU +17.6%); decelerates as AI-interactive penetration (21.6% of 236 brand customers) matures and the fragmented FMCG marketing market (0.9% share, #5) caps share gains; 3% from year 8.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC, pre-lease, ex-FV-gains EBITDA: FY2024 25.2%, FY2025 20.2% (R&D +75%), H1 FY2026 25.1%. Base 23.5-24% assumes the H1 FY2026 expense-ratio gain is mostly held, with a drift to 23% as competition and ECL charges (2.1% of revenue) normalise. Includes the ~RMB35m/yr receivables impairment.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2025 capex RMB10.8m (0.65%) and H1 FY2026 nil, against PP&E depreciation of RMB49.5m (3.0%): the terminal fleet is being run down and management says growth will not rely on large-scale new sites. Capex ramps from 1.5% to converge with D&A at 2.5% by year 5 so the terminal network is replaced, not harvested.
base.tax_rationale: Shanghai Quna holds HNTE 15% status to December 2028; FY2025 effective 11.4%, cash 6.7% of PBT, H1 FY2026 cash 12.3%. Ramps to 20% from year 6 as a blend of the 25% statutory rate and a non-renewed or partially renewed HNTE.
base.wc_rationale: Trade receivables are 36% of revenue (131-day DSO) and grew RMB124.6m on RMB323.7m of FY2025 revenue growth; payables and contract liabilities offset only a little. FY2025 net WC of ~+2m was a one-off prepayment unwind; FY2024 was -164m. Negative capture of 30% of the revenue change.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 10%/2.5% implies 13.7x; the 12x cap binds, reflecting a small-cap project-based marketing business in a fragmented market.

bull.rationale: AI interactive marketing (93% GM) keeps compounding and penetration rises from 22% toward 50%+ of a growing brand base; KA ARPU keeps rising; H1 FY2026 operating leverage extends to a 28% EBITDA margin (above the FY2024 25% peak); HNTE renewed through the horizon; DSO improves as engagements shift to annual contracts. Dubai/Singapore entertainment given no value.

bear.rationale: FMCG marketing budgets are cut as China consumer stimulus (trade-in subsidies, 'debut economy') fades; two or three of the 29 KA customers (67% of H1 FY2026 revenue) re-tender away; digital retail media and larger AI vendors commoditise interactive terminals; revenue falls 5% over FY2028-29 and S&D/R&D cannot be cut in step, margin to 13%; HNTE lost at the 2028 renewal (25% from year 4); receivables collection worsens (35% capture, with the ECL charge inside the margin). Still cash-generative, so the terminal value does not hit the zero floor.

scenario_narratives.base: Qunabox keeps growing its marketing-services revenue at 20% in FY2026 decelerating to GDP-like rates by year 8, as AI interactive services (RMB131.6m in H1 FY2026, +102%, 93% gross margin, 21.6% penetration of 236 brand customers) are cross-sold into the installed terminal network without large new-site capex. EBITDA margin settles around 23-24%, between the FY2025 trough (20.2%, R&D step-up) and the H1 FY2026 run-rate (25.1%). Capex is rebuilt from today's near-zero to match depreciation so the terminal fleet is replaced; cash tax ramps from the HNTE-aided 12% to 20%; receivables keep absorbing 30% of every incremental RMB of revenue. The RMB1.1bn net cash and RMB337m of wealth-management products are credited at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI interactive penetration climbs toward half the brand base, KA ARPU keeps rising double digits, new verticals (NEVs, appliances, cosmetics) add customers, and the H1 FY2026 operating leverage carries the EBITDA margin to 28%. Growth of 24% in FY2026 fades to 3% only by year 10. HNTE status is renewed through the horizon and DSO improves as engagements move to annual contracts. No value is given to the Dubai Holox JV or Singapore entertainment projects.
scenario_narratives.bear: The business is a project-based, campaign-tendered marketing vendor with 0.9% share in a fragmented market and two-thirds of revenue from 29 key accounts. A China consumer slowdown and the end of subsidy-driven product launches cut brand budgets; several KA accounts re-tender to digital retail media or cheaper AI-content vendors; revenue stalls in FY2027 and falls 5% over FY2028-29, the EBITDA margin compresses to 13% because S&D and R&D are sticky, the HNTE concession is lost in 2028 (25% tax), and receivable quality deteriorates. The company remains cash-generative and the cash pile is intact, so even the bear value sits well above the current price; the one outcome none of the three scenarios models is a balance-sheet integrity or repatriation failure, which is the only reading that reconciles today's price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 40%: a thin two-year post-IPO record, 67% of revenue from 29 key accounts in a discretionary, cyclical budget line, 131-day DSO with RMB35m/yr impairments, an HNTE tax concession that expires in 2028, a Cayman/HK holdco over onshore RMB cash that has never paid a dividend, and a 95% share-price collapse over twelve months with no disclosed cause, which says the market does not believe the accounts or expects the cash never to reach shareholders. Bull cut to 20% because it needs AI-interactive penetration, KA ARPU, margin expansion and HNTE renewal all to go right at once. Base 40%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a conservatively framed, components-built margin, with all non-operating income (interest, wealth-management fair-value gains) stripped from the flows and its source assets credited once in the bridge. The arithmetic result is that the business is worth several times the current price in every scenario, because the issued-share market capitalisation (~HK$1.75bn) is below net cash plus liquid wealth-management products (~HK$1.68bn) and the operating business is generating roughly RMB300m of owner FCF a year. That gap is the finding, not the thesis: a 95% drawdown with no profit warning, no suspension and no subsequent-event disclosure means the market is pricing either a failure of the balance sheet as reported, or a permanent inability of a Hong Kong-listed Cayman holdco to get onshore RMB cash to shareholders (no dividend has ever been paid; the FY2025 buyback was RMB18m against RMB1.5bn of cash). None of the three scenarios models that outcome; the DCF value is conditional on the accounts being true and the cash being accessible. Before any position, verify the cash and wealth-management balances against the auditor's report and bank confirmations, check for undisclosed pledges or related-party flows, and look for any capital-return commitment. A return of capital (special dividend or substantial buyback) would be the catalyst that forces the market to re-price the cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Balance-sheet integrity and cash accessibility: ~RMB1.95bn of cash and wealth-management products held onshore under a Cayman holdco that has never paid a dividend; the valuation is mostly this cash plus a 12x terminal multiple on a thin operating record. The 95% share-price collapse is unexplained by any disclosure.
Customer concentration: 29 KA customers = 67% of H1 FY2026 revenue; project-based, re-tendered each cycle, tied to discretionary FMCG new-product budgets and to Chinese consumer stimulus policy.
Receivables: 131-day DSO, RMB672m trade receivables at 30 Jun 2026 (RMB778m gross), RMB35m/yr ECL charges, growth absorbs ~30% of incremental revenue in working capital.
Tax: HNTE 15% concession runs to December 2028; loss moves the cash rate to 25%.

Capex under-investment: FY2025 capex 0.65% of revenue and nil in H1 FY2026 against 3% depreciation; the model rebuilds capex to 2.5%, but if terminal retirements are not replaced the revenue base erodes.
Competition and obsolescence: 0.9% share of a fragmented outdoor FMCG marketing market; larger AI/retail-media platforms could commoditise interactive terminals.
Execution drag from the Dubai/Singapore 'physical AI entertainment' pivot and planned M&A, both excluded from the flows but a potential use of the cash the valuation credits.
Currency: RMB flows against an HKD quote; a 10% RMB depreciation moves the HKD value one-for-one.
